title: Super+Tab opens a picker of workspaces
body:
Workspaces are designed in decade-4c2624. Jack wants no key that jumps straight to a given workspace. One key opens a picker instead.

## Proposal

- Super+Tab opens a grid of workspaces in the viewer. It joins decade's keys in Jack's `~/.config/hypr/decade.lua`. Hyprland's own Super+Tab is already unbound there.
- The cells are in creation order. Dragging a cell moves it. The picker never sorts by recency.
- Each cell shows its workspace's panes scaled down, with the workspace's name drawn below the cell. Under the text rule in CLAUDE.md, decade leaves its own chrome text out of the scaled render. Text inside client windows scales with them.
- Arrow keys or Ctrl+H/J/K/L move, Enter or a click switches, and Esc closes. A last cell, "+ New workspace", starts the palette's new-workspace flow. Each cell has an x that closes its workspace after a confirmation.
- While any viewer has the picker open, decade sends frame callbacks to the clients of workspaces no viewer shows, twice a second, so their renders stay fresh. With no picker open, those clients get no frame callbacks. Jack asked for care here, so the tick is limited to that case.
close_reason: Landed in 5118c09. Pane outlines were left out of the cells at Jack's request. Super+Tab was added to the decade keys in ~/.config/hypr/decade.lua.
